findings.text: Misc format exec probe validates that no loader is already staged, that the per namespace control is enabled, and that a handler matches the current executable description. On success it selects an interpreter name and invocation attributes, then follows one of three courses: staging an interpreter file for a later format and declining, preserving arguments for transparent handling, or constructing fresh arguments for ordinary handling, before recording the interpreter and reporting acceptance or a negative failure.

Invocation mode determines how the executable description is updated. Loader mode opens the chosen interpreter immediately, stores the resulting file separately from the main interpreter slot, and declines so scanning continues. Transparent mode skips argument construction and marks the description only after the interpreter opens successfully. Ordinary mode builds new arguments, updates the recorded interpreter name, opens the interpreter, and optionally records desires for an execution file descriptor and credential use.

Interpreter name replacement releases the previous name unless it aliases the original file name, then stores a duplicate of the supplied name. Allocation failure is reported and leaves no name. Success reports zero.

Registration field scanning advances to a caller chosen delimiter, terminates the field, and validates escape sequences by requiring paired hexadecimal digits after a specific introduction, failing otherwise. Magic style matching parses a decimal offset when present, extracts raw magic and mask spans, decodes hexadecimal escapes in place, requires equal decoded lengths when a mask exists, and enforces that size and offset fit within the initial executable buffer.

Registration input begins with a delimiter byte followed by name, kind, match, interpreter and flag sections padded to ease scanning. Total length is bounded below and above. Names must be non empty and must avoid single dot, double dot and slash. A delimiter that itself denotes a flag is rejected. Trailing newline is optional but all bytes must be consumed.

Kind selection distinguishes extension, magic and programmable matching. Programmable matching requires a build option, mandates empty offset and match sections, treats the interpreter section as a handler name that must be non empty, and forbids fixed invocation attributes because they are decided per execution. Extension matching skips offset and mask and requires a slash free token. Magic matching uses the dedicated offset and pattern parser.

Flag tail is consumed until an unrecognized character. Certain combinations are rejected: transparency with argument zero preservation, and loader mode with transparency, argument preservation, credential use or binary descriptor passing. When the interpreter is opened at execution time against caller context without preopening, loader or credential modes require an absolute path. A disabled directive clears itself and creates the entry disabled for later activation. New entries start with a single reference.
The control command length bound is three, limiting accepted management writes.

Management writes encode four operations: empty input is ignored, zero disables, one enables, and minus one removes. An optional final newline is stripped before comparison. Inputs longer than the bound or with other content are rejected. User memory is copied through a bounded stack buffer sized one beyond the bound before parsing.

Status rendering reports enabled or disabled state, then either programmable handler identity plus each bound interpreter name and path under read side protection, or the plain interpreter path. It then lists active flag letters, followed by match details: dotted extension, or numeric offset with hexadecimal encoded magic and optional mask. Sequential output appends only while capacity remains and otherwise records overflow by pinning fill to capacity; single character output silently drops when full, and constant string output optimizes single character and general cases.

Inode creation obtains storage through filesystem specific allocation when offered else a generic cache, performs mandatory initialization, and on success enrolls the object on the owning superblock list. The control helper then assigns a fresh number, caller supplied mode, and current timestamps. Failures propagate as null.

When mandatory initialization fails after allocation, the filesystem destroy hook runs when present, then release is deferred to a callback that invokes the filesystem free hook when available else returns the object to the generic cache.

Membership of entries in the search structure is serialized by a dedicated spin lock, with removal using a deferred reclamation variant and eviction checking hashed state before removal. Superblock inode list insertion is serialized by its own lock. Bound interpreter iteration for status display runs under read side protection while the open file pins the entry, so protection addresses tearing rather than lifetime.

Recursive directory teardown holds a nested write lock on each level, marks visited directories dead, updates times and clears links while locked, invalidates and discards dentries, emits deletion notifications, and adjusts parent times and links on completion. Child discovery holds the parent lock, briefly nests the child lock to obtain a referenced child, then releases before descending.

Entries transition from staged and unhashed to published on first enable, remain searchable while enabled, and leave via explicit removal, bulk removal, unlink, or inode eviction. Single removal takes the parent lock and only unhashes when the dentry remains hashed. Bulk removal walks directory children to include staged entries and skips control files without private state. Unlink rejects control files, unhashes, then delegates to simple removal that updates timestamps and link counts. Eviction clears the inode, unhashes when still linked, and drops the handler reference.

Control directory operations provide lookup and a custom unlink that enforces entry ownership. Entry files open through a single display helper that binds the entry as display context and restores write capability for command writes after sequence initialization clears it. Sequence initialization allocates zeroed state, links file and operation table, initializes the internal lock, and constrains object lifetime to the file.

Link management decrements with a warning on zero or clears unconditionally, accounting each transition that reaches zero. Positivity requires both a positive state and a hashed state. Sibling traversal safely converts hash links. Deletion notification adds a directory marker when appropriate. The locked removal wrapper always selects the locked variant of the shared recursive helper.

Several orderings avoid leaks or mis execution. The transparent marker is set only after successful interpreter opening so a declined match does not leak it. Loader open decline is converted to an access failure to prevent falling back to the embedded interpreter. Staged execution arguments are rejected with loader or transparent modes because no argument vector exists to receive them. Registration rejects flag valued delimiters, pads with delimiters to simplify parsing, bounds decoded pattern size against the exec buffer, and stops decoding at embedded nulls.

Observed state includes executable descriptions carrying loader file, main interpreter file, interpreter name versus file name aliasing, transparent marker, and flags for descriptor passing and credential use; registration entries carrying name, kind flags, offset, magic, mask, size, interpreter or handler identity, interpreter list, hash node, dentry and reference count; sequence files carrying fill, capacity, buffer, file link, operation table and lock; inodes carrying number, mode, link count and superblock linkage.

Non static helpers available across files include interpreter name replacement, sequential output formatting and overflow handling, single display open and sequence open, inode allocation with superblock enrollment and link count management, discardable marking, child iteration, simple unlink, and locked recursive removal.
